# neo.mjs's postinstall calls a devDependency, so consumer installs fail

## Context

Found while dry-running the v13.2 deploy for #19047: the pages pipeline installs the engine as an npm dependency, so I installed engine `dev` the same way. It fails before any build step runs.

**Reproduced 2026-09-22 on `dev@e66b6f8142`:**

```
git worktree add --detach <wt> origin/dev
cd <wt> && npm pack --ignore-scripts            # neo.mjs-13.1.0.tgz, 5,714 files
mkdir <consumer> && cd <consumer>
echo '{"name":"c","version":"1.0.0","private":true}' > package.json
npm install <wt>/neo.mjs-13.1.0.tgz
→ npm error code 127
→ npm error command sh -c neo-agent-skills-materialize
→ npm error sh: neo-agent-skills-materialize: command not found
```

## The Problem

`package.json` declares `"postinstall": "neo-agent-skills-materialize"`, and `neo-agent-skills` is a **devDependency**. npm runs a dependency's `postinstall` inside every consumer's install, and a consumer never installs its dependencies' devDependencies. So the binary exists where the hook runs **only if the consumer's own tree supplies it**.

**No published version carries it yet.** `neo.mjs@13.1.0` (npm, 2026-07-03) has no `postinstall`; the hook arrived on `dev` on 2026-08-26 via `#17799`. Measured 2026-09-22 with packed tarballs (npm 11):

| Consumer shape | `dev` | this fix |
|---|---|---|
| empty project, `npm install <tgz>` | exit 127 | exit 0 |
| `create-app` scaffold as generated today (`postinstall: cd node_modules/neo.mjs && npm i`) — the same order as pages' step 4 (install) → step 7 (`npm i` on neo) | exit 127: the outer install fires the hook before the consumer's own `npm i` on neo runs | exit 0; the nested `npm i` runs `prepare` and materializes 37 links inside `node_modules/neo.mjs` |
| a workspace that declares `neo-agent-skills` itself, with no hook of its own | exit 0, **and** 37 links projected at the workspace root — the dependency script finds the consumer's `.bin`, and `INIT_CWD` is the consumer root | exit 0, 0 links — the workspace runs the materializer itself |

So 13.2.0 would break every default-scripts install whose tree lacks `neo-agent-skills`: pages (step 4 dies before step 7), devindex (declares no skills), today's `create-app` scaffold, and third-party projects. (pnpm and bun block dependency lifecycle scripts by default.)

The last row is a behaviour this fix removes, not only a failure it cures: on `dev`, a consumer that happens to carry the skills gets them projected into its root by the engine. **Fork resolved: consumer-owned projection.** The alternative — an engine `postinstall` script that runs the materializer only when `neo-agent-skills` resolves from the installing tree — was put to @neo-gpt at @tobiu's suggestion, and rejected: that root projection is an incidental cross-package effect of the engine's hook, not a promise `#17798` makes to consumers (it gives each consumer its own dependency and materializer), and keeping it would preserve an engine-controlled write into a consumer's tree. *Corrected 2026-09-22: the first version of this section claimed every default-scripts install would fail.*

## The Architectural Reality

- `#17798` chose install-time materialization so each repository that *uses* the skills gets projected links in its own checkout. That intent is right. What it missed is that `neo.mjs` is also a *published package*, so its own install hook fires in other people's installs.
- npm already separates the two contexts: **a registry or tarball install never runs `prepare`, while a dependency's `postinstall` runs in every consumer's install.** `prepare` does run on an argument-less `npm install` / `npm ci` in the package's own directory, on pack/publish, and for Git-dependency and linked-folder installs, which build from a checkout ([npm v11 scripts](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v11/using-npm/scripts/)); neither of the last two is a supported way to consume `neo.mjs`, and neither was measured here. The engine's own-checkout lifecycle already lives in `prepare`: `buildScripts/util/prepare.mjs` (`runPrepare`), which short-circuits on `--package-lock-only` and resolves husky from its manifest's `bin` so it works under `cmd.exe`.
- The materializer finds its target through `INIT_CWD` (`materialize-harness-skills.mjs` `consumerRoot()`), which npm sets identically for `prepare`, so the projection lands in the same place.
- `neo-agent-brain` is unaffected on its own: it is `private`, and `neo-agent-skills` is a regular dependency there.

## The Fix

1. `package.json` — delete `scripts.postinstall`.
2. `buildScripts/util/prepare.mjs` — generalize `resolveHuskyBin` into a package-and-bin resolver, and give `runPrepare` a second stage after husky: `neo-agent-skills-materialize`, resolved from `node_modules/neo-agent-skills/package.json` `bin`, launched through `process.execPath`. The lock-only guard still returns before either stage; a materializer failure fails the install, as husky's does.
3. `test/playwright/unit/buildScripts/prepare.spec.mjs` — *"husky is the only Engine prepare step"* becomes husky-then-materializer; add the failure, missing-package and missing-bin arms.
4. Comments that name `postinstall` as the materialization path (`.gitignore`, `.github/workflows/substrate-sync.yml`, `.github/workflows/guard-ci-parity-lint.yml`) say `prepare`.
5. Consequence for consumers: one that wants skills runs `neo-agent-skills-materialize` from its own lifecycle — `#17798`'s consumer contract, which the Brain already follows. For `create-app`, that line travels with the devDependency sync in neomjs/create-app#34.

## Contract Ledger

| Target surface | Source of authority | Proposed behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `package.json` `scripts.postinstall` | `#17798` mechanism | removed | — | `prepare.mjs` docblock | consumer probe above: exit 127 |
| `buildScripts/util/prepare.mjs` `runPrepare` | the engine's own-checkout lifecycle | lock-only guard → husky → materializer; either failure fails the install | `npm ci --ignore-scripts` skips it, as before — `substrate-sync.yml`'s `--check` stays the arm | docblock | `prepare.spec.mjs` |
| a registry or tarball install of `neo.mjs` | npm lifecycle semantics | runs no engine script | — | — | the same probe, exit 0 |

## Decision Record impact

`amends #17798 AC-2`, narrowly and for the Engine only. That AC required `neomjs/neo`, the Brain and devindex each to run the materializer from `postinstall`; the Engine moves it to `prepare` because it is also a published package, and the consumer-install falsifier above is why. Everything else `#17798` settled stands: the consumer-owned dependency and projection, the Brain's and devindex's own hooks, and the `--check` arm. No ADR is involved. (@neo-gpt's source-of-authority read, R1 preflight on PR #19053.)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1 — `package.json` has no `postinstall`; `runPrepare` runs the materializer after husky, resolved from `neo-agent-skills`'s `bin` declaration.
- [ ] AC-2 — The reproducer above, run against the branch, exits 0. On `dev` it exits 127 — red first, then green.
- [ ] AC-3 — The engine's own checkout still materializes: a bare `npm ci` leaves `npx --no-install neo-agent-skills-materialize --check` green, and `npm install --package-lock-only` runs neither stage.
- [ ] AC-4 — `prepare.spec.mjs` covers the stage order, a materializer failure failing the install, and a missing package or bin entry as a named error.

## Out of Scope

- Whether the published tarball should carry materialized links at all (`npm publish` runs after `npm ci`, with or without this change) — that belongs to `check-package-contents.yml`'s gate.
- The pages topology — `D#19050`.

## Avoided Traps

- **Moving `neo-agent-skills` into `dependencies`.** Consumer installs pass, but every library user downloads agent substrate and runs the materializer against their own project root via `INIT_CWD`.
- **A shell guard (`command -v … || true`).** POSIX-only — `prepare.mjs` exists because `cmd.exe` has no `[` — and it would swallow a real materializer failure in the engine's own checkout.
- **Detecting "am I a dependency?" in a script.** Re-implements what npm's `prepare`/`postinstall` split already encodes.

## Related

- #19047 — its AC-4 dry run installs the engine as a dependency, so it cannot pass until this lands
- `#17798` — origin of the hook (closed)
